findings.title: 2 tracking companies not named in the privacy policy
findings.detail: The policy names 2 companies. We saw these and found no mention: Google, Tealium. (The policy may describe them only by category, e.g. 'advertising partners'.)
findings.law: UK GDPR Art. 13(1)(e) (you must be told who receives your data)

findings.severity_note: Lowered from high: no substantial advertising or session-replay evidence cited (a tracking cookie, activity after reject, or 3+ requests to an actual tracking domain; a tag loader like Google Tag Manager alone doesn't count), so an exemption or innocent explanation is plausible.
findings.title: Google advertising tracking started before consent
findings.detail: Three Google advertising-tracker requests were recorded before the visitor had given consent. This indicates non-essential advertising tracking began without prior consent.
findings.law: PECR reg. 6; UK GDPR Articles 5(1)(a) and 7
findings.reasoning: PECR generally requires prior consent for advertising cookies or similar tracking. The site's cookie policy expressly says advertising cookies require consent, so the observed pre-consent advertising requests also create a direct contradiction with the site's own policy. This is high severity because the evidence identifies the activity as advertising tracking.
findings.law_eu: ePrivacy Directive 2002/58/EC Art. 5(3) (consent before storing/reading on a device); EU GDPR Articles 5(1)(a) and 7

findings.title: Analytics tracking started before consent
findings.detail: Seven Tealium analytics-tracker requests were recorded before the visitor had given consent. The audit cannot show from the URLs alone whether information was stored or read on the device, but the activity appears inconsistent with the site's stated consent requirement for performance cookies.
findings.law: PECR reg. 6; UK GDPR Articles 5(1)(a) and 7
findings.reasoning: Analytics may in some circumstances fall within a limited statutory exception, but that cannot be confirmed from the evidence and the site says consent is required. Medium severity is appropriate because an innocent technical explanation or an applicable analytics exception remains plausible.
findings.law_eu: ePrivacy Directive 2002/58/EC Art. 5(3) (consent before storing/reading on a device); EU GDPR Articles 5(1)(a) and 7

findings.title: Accept is one click, but we found no way to reject
findings.detail: The banner offers "ACCEPT ALL", but our automated check could not find any reject or decline option. (This may be a limit of our check, so treat it as something to verify.)
findings.law: ICO cookie guidance (refusing must be as easy as accepting)
findings.law_eu: EDPB Guidelines 05/2020 on consent; EDPB Cookie Banner Taskforce report (2023)

ai_review.summary: The audit indicates that Google advertising tracking and Tealium analytics activity began before consent was obtained. The advertising activity is a high-severity concern because it is clearly identified as advertising tracking and contradicts the cookie policy's consent requirement; the analytics issue is medium because the precise device-level activity and any applicable exception cannot be confirmed from the listed URLs. The rejection option could not be successfully tested, but that automated issue is not repeated here.
evidence: E1: Cookie banner found: True. Reject clicked successfully: False. Method: failed. Buttons clicked: CUSTOMIZE.
E2: Tracker Google (Advertising): 3 requests before consent, 0 after reject, to googletagmanager.com.
E3: Tracker Tealium (Analytics): 7 requests before consent, 0 after reject, to tiqcdn.com.

E4: Privacy policy: https://www.gsk.com/en-gb/investors/shareholder-information/privacy-notice-for-ordinary-shareholders/. Companies it names: Computershare Investor Services PLC, Computershare Group entities. Contact email found: dataprotection@computershare.co.uk.

E6: Automated check (medium): 2 tracking companies not named in the privacy policy. The policy names 2 companies. We saw these and found no mention: Google, Tealium. (The policy may describe them only by category, e.g. 'advertising partners'.)

E7: Automated check (low): Accept is one click, but we found no way to reject. The banner offers "ACCEPT ALL", but our automated check could not find any reject or decline option. (This may be a limit of our check, so treat it as something to verify.)
